Standing Counsel
 Coram:
 Justice S.K. Sahoo
 Order
This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the State.
This is an application for bail.

The appellant-petitioner has been convicted under section 450/376(2)(f)(i)/313 of the Indian Penal Code and section 6 of the POCSO Act read with section 3(1)(xii) of the S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act and sentenced to undergo R.I. for a period of ten years and to pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand), in default, to further undergo R.I. for a // 2 // period of six months for the offence under section 376(2)(f)(i) of the Indian Penal Code, R.I. for a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.4,000/- (rupees four thousand), in default, to further undergo R.I. for a period of six months for the offence under section 450 of the Indian Penal Code, R.I. for a period of five years and to pay a fine of Rs.4,000/- (rupees four thousand), in default, to further undergo R.I. for a period of six Raghunandan Das @ Rajib vs State Of Odisha on 14 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158438126/
1 months for the offence under section 313 of the Indian Penal Code and R.I. for a period of one year and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/- (rupees one thousand), in default, to further undergo R.I. for a period of three months for the offence under section 3(1)(xii) of the S.C. & S.T. (PoA) Act and no separate punishment is awarded under section 6 of the POCSO Act in view of section 42 of the said Act and all the substantive sentences were directed to run concurrently by the learned Additional Sessions Judge -cum- Special Court under POCSO Act, Puri in T.R. Case No.51 of 2015.
Considering the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner is in judicial custody for eight years out of ten years of substantive sentence imposed by the learned trial Court and even though paper book has been prepared but there is no chance of early hearing of // 3 // the appeal in the near future and taking into account the petitioner is a local man, there is no chance of absconding and he was granted interim bail for a period of three months and after availing the same, he surrendered at right time, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
Let the appellant-petitioner be released on bail pending disposal of the appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty thousand) with two solvent sureties each for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial Court with such terms and conditions as the learned Court may deem just and proper.
